title: Vodafone Idea Reaffirms $4.7 Billion Capex Plan, Targets Double-Digit Revenue Growth
excerpt: India's third-largest telecom operator doubled down on its three-year turnaround plan during a Q1 earnings call, citing progress on funding, network rollout, and subscriber retention after years of losses.
body:
• Vodafone Idea reaffirmed a ₹45,000 crore ($4.72 billion) capital expenditure plan over three years, targeting double-digit revenue growth and a tripling of cash EBITDA.
  • The company has already raised a ₹6,400 crore funding tranche and placed network equipment orders worth approximately ₹9,000 crore.
  • Vi plans to deploy 3,500 new 4G sites per month, complete its 4G rollout across 17 key circles in 18 months, and expand 5G to over 200 cities in the next two quarters.
  • The telecom operator reported a narrower first-quarter loss, aided by higher average revenue per user, as it works to recover from a debt crisis that left the government with a nearly 50% stake.

Vodafone Idea reaffirmed its ambitious three-year growth targets during a first-quarter earnings call, pledging to invest ₹45,000 crore ($4.72 billion) in its network, deliver double-digit revenue growth, and triple its cash EBITDA, according to Reuters. CEO Abhijit Kishore said the company has the financial architecture in place to support its turnaround roadmap.

Funding and Equipment Orders

The telecom operator, India's third-largest by subscribers, has already secured a ₹6,400 crore funding tranche and is pursuing additional capital from public and private Indian banks as well as foreign lenders. Network equipment orders worth approximately ₹9,000 crore have been placed, with execution expected within the next two quarters or less.

"The continued support from the promoters and our ongoing conversation with various sets of lenders gives us the confidence that we have the financial architecture in place to support our roadmap."

— Abhijit Kishore, CEO, Vodafone Idea

The capex will be funded primarily through debt, targeting ₹25,000 crore in bank funding and ₹10,000 crore in non-funded facilities. The company has ruled out an equity raise at this stage, stating its current funding structure is adequate.

Network Rollout Plans

Vi plans to deploy approximately 3,500 new 4G sites per month and complete its 4G rollout across 17 priority circles — which contribute over 99% of revenue — within about 18 months. The company also aims to expand 5G services to more than 200 additional cities over the next two quarters, building on its existing 5G presence in multiple cities.

The 17-5-5 strategy focuses on regaining coverage parity with rivals Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel in priority markets, converting remaining 2G sites to 4G in other circles, and achieving seamless 5G coverage in urban areas with populations above 20,000. Satellite communication through a partnership with AST SpaceMobile will be used to extend coverage to remote, rural, maritime, and border regions.

Q1 Results Show Progress

Vodafone Idea reported a narrower first-quarter loss compared to the preceding March quarter, helped by higher average revenue per user. In Q4 FY26, the company had reported a net loss of ₹5,521 crore on revenue of ₹11,332 crore, with ARPU of ₹174. EBITDA for that quarter stood at ₹4,889 crore, an annual increase of 4.9%.

The subscriber base has shown signs of stabilization. In Q4 FY26, the 4G/5G subscriber base grew to 128.9 million, while the overall subscriber base held flat at 192.8 million. Bank debt fell sharply to ₹726 crore by March 2026, down from ₹2,326 crore a year earlier.

A Long Road Back

Vodafone Idea was formed in 2018 through a merger of Vodafone India and Aditya Birla Group's Idea Cellular. The company has reported losses every quarter since, weighed down by over $22 billion in total debt — including deferred spectrum payments and adjusted gross revenue (AGR) liabilities owed to the government.

The debt crisis eventually led to the Indian government becoming Vi's single largest shareholder, holding a nearly 50% stake since 2025 after converting deferred spectrum and AGR dues into equity. In a key reprieve, the government granted a decade-long deferment on AGR payments, giving Vi breathing room to invest in its network.

Despite the turnaround signals, the company trails its larger rivals by wide margins. Jio's ARPU stands at ₹211, Airtel's at ₹256, while Vi's is around ₹174. The gap in 5G coverage is even wider, with Jio and Airtel having launched 5G across hundreds of cities while Vi is still in early stages.

What's Next

The three-year plan reaffirmed this week was first outlined in January 2026, when Vi announced the ₹45,000 crore capex commitment alongside its Q3 FY26 results. With equipment orders placed and funding partially secured, execution over the next 12–18 months will determine whether Vi can convert its turnaround plan into actual subscriber and revenue recovery in one of the world's most competitive telecom markets.
